hints_cache: This is a range query problem in disguise. You need to efficiently update a value (adding an obstacle) and query a maximum (the largest available gap) over a specific distance.
Think about what changes when you add an obstacle at point X. You are essentially splitting one large gap into two smaller gaps. You need a way to track these 'gap lengths' across the number line.

To answer the rug query for range [0, x], you need the maximum of two things: the largest gap between any two obstacles before x, and the distance between the very last obstacle before x and x itself.

A Segment Tree or Binary Indexed Tree can store the maximum gap lengths. Use a sorted set or a balanced BST to quickly find the immediate neighbors of a new obstacle so you know which gaps are being created or destroyed.

Map the coordinate system to your tree. When an obstacle is added at p, update the tree at position p with the distance to the obstacle immediately to its left. To query x, find the max value in the tree up to x and compare it (and the final tail segment) to the required size.
